items.title: Show HN: Making a smart TV dumb and then smart
items.description: A recent (unwanted) webOS update that got installed on TV prompted me to start going down the rabbit hole of writing new TV software. After a couple of weekends and massive help from 4 different models, finally managed to get v1 working. My daughter enjoys navigating TV through speech while I get to browse on the biggest screen at home. While all of the code was written by ML models, there were decisions I had to help with. In specific: using WebRTC to cut down latency, repurposing vendor logic for buffering voice samples and designing user experience. It was liberating to finally free the TV of bloatware and make it truly personalized! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50202865 Points: 50 # Comments: 13

items.title: Ask HN: If the models are so good, why doesn't OpenAI just start 100 companies?
items.description: Title is a bit of an exaggeration but the question is more: if the frontier models are so good, why even sell them as your primary money maker? Couldn't OpenAI or Anthropic make a lot more money by just starting companies themselves that leverage the models and building their own products? Is selling tokens really the best strategy? Especially with commodification and prices declining wouldn't that indicate there is more money to be made on the application-side of the models rather than the utility side Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50200997 Points: 247 # Comments: 257
